question: A 2 kg block on a rough 30 degree incline is connected by a taut massless rope parallel to the incline, over a frictionless pulley, to a hanging 3 kg mass. The incline block is currently sliding downslope. Its kinetic friction coefficient is 0.20; use g = 10 m/s^2. Draw the free-body diagrams and calculate the acceleration direction and magnitude and the tension while it is still sliding downslope. Explain the direction of friction.

lawIds: constraint of inextensible rope over pulley (equal acceleration magnitude)

assumptions: massless rope and frictionless pulley so tension is uniform
kinetic friction applies because block is sliding
positive direction taken up the incline for block / downward for hanging mass

qualitativeClaims.claim: Kinetic friction on the incline block acts up the slope, opposing its current downslope sliding.
The hanging mass accelerates downward and the incline block accelerates up the slope while it is still sliding downslope (decelerating).
qualitativeClaims.expected: a = +3.31 m/s^2 up-slope for block, downward for hanging mass

qualitativeClaims.claim: FBD block: weight m1*g down, normal N perpendicular to plane, tension T up-slope, kinetic friction f_k up-slope.
FBD hanging mass: weight m2*g down, tension T up.
Equations: m2*g - T = m2*a; T - m1*g*sin30 - f_k = m1*a.
